body:
The current title and text are out-of-date and do not correspond to the current requirement. Following discussion, the intent is to reorient the section around existing 3.7.1: requirements here should mitigate the risk/impact of attacks where the attacker is able to abuse the user's session (either they have the session token, or they indirectly utilize it through CSRF and related attackes).

Proposal:

### V3.7 Defenses Against Session Abuse

This section provides requirements to mitigate the risk posed by active session that are either hijacked or abused through vectors such as cross-site attacks.

I think the sections *could* be combined in some way, but 3.7.1 is unrelated to session termination. Perhaps the sections could be combined into some sort of "defenses against session theft" section, but I think "session termination" 

@jmanico Agreed, so IMO it makes sense to iterate quickly on section text to simply capture the overall intent of a section.
